title: 明日から教えてやる  (I Will Teach You Starting Tomorrow)

segments.t: Following his boss's orders, Muranishi approaches Ono, the company's star salesman. Instead of talking about encyclopedias, Ono tests Muranishi on Alfred Hitchcock, pop music, and singing in the street. Listen to how this strange audition unfolds.
あの、小野さんから営業のことを学べって。
ヒッチコックが死んだよ。
無愛想ですね。
正気か？お前。
サイコは傑作ですよ。
お前、音楽は何を聴くんだよ？
最近は洋楽です。
日本人ならこれだろ。歌えよ。
僕らは自由だね。
よし、合格だ。明日から教えてやるよ。
よろしくお願いします。
じゃあ、さようなら。
Ono speaks in rapid, confident plain speech while Muranishi stays respectful. Let's walk through the highlights.
あの、小野さんから営業のことを学べって。

'Um, I was told to learn about sales from you, Ono-san.' Opening with "ano" buys a polite beat before making a request. "Eigyou" means sales work, and ending on casual quoting "tte" acts like 'they told me to...'.
ヒッチコックが死んだよ。
'Hitchcock died.' "Shinda" is the plain past of "shinu", to die, and "yo" flags it as fresh news the listener has not heard yet.
無愛想ですね。
'That is rather blunt, is it not?' Muranishi mistakes the remark for coldness and says "buaisou", unfriendly or curt, softened with "desu ne".
正気か？お前。
'Are you out of your mind?' Ono's favourite catchphrase hinges on "shouki", sanity or right mind. Adding sharp "ka" fires back 'are you sane?' whenever someone says something outrageous.
お前、音楽は何を聴くんだよ？
'What kind of music do you listen to?' "Ongaku" means music, "nani" asks what, and "kiku" covers both listening and asking.
最近は洋楽です。
'Lately, Western music.' "Saikin" means lately or recently. "Yougaku" pairs "you", Western, with "gaku", music—contrasting neatly with "hougaku", Japanese music.
日本人ならこれだろ。
'If you are Japanese, it has to be this.' Adding "jin", person, to "Nihon" builds "Nihonjin", a Japanese person, and "nara" means 'if it is the case that'.
僕らは自由だね。
'We are free, are we not?' Singing along, Muranishi uses "bokura", casual 'we', and "jiyuu", freedom—a word that echoes through the whole episode.
よし、合格だ。
'All right, you pass.' "Yoshi" is an upbeat 'all right!', and "goukaku" is the word for passing an exam or audition.
明日から教えてやるよ。

'I will teach you starting tomorrow.' "Ashita" is tomorrow, followed by "kara", from. "Oshiete yaru" attaches tough, big-brother "yaru" to "oshieru", to teach, showing Ono sees himself as the boss of this pair.
よろしくお願いします。

'Thank you, I look forward to working with you.' Built around "yoroshiku", favourably, "yoroshiku onegai shimasu" is the set greeting you use whenever a new partnership, job, or lesson begins. Now let's listen to Ono's impromptu audition once more.
あの、小野さんから営業のことを学べって。
ヒッチコックが死んだよ。
無愛想ですね。
正気か？お前。
サイコは傑作ですよ。
お前、音楽は何を聴くんだよ？
最近は洋楽です。
日本人ならこれだろ。歌えよ。
僕らは自由だね。
よし、合格だ。明日から教えてやるよ。
よろしくお願いします。
じゃあ、さようなら。
You just heard "saikin" for lately, "jiyuu" for free, "ashita kara" for starting tomorrow, and the indispensable partnership greeting "yoroshiku onegai shimasu". Until next time.
また明日。
